daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The leadership of the Nahdlatul Ulama (NU), Indonesia's largest Islamic organization, is being decided today as the election for Rais Aam and Ketua Umum takes place during the organization's national congress (Muktamar). The selection proceeds without formal candidate registration, following NU's traditional internal process. Two members of the AHWA body are predicted to be re-elected, and there are differing views on the selection mechanism within the congress proceedings.

  • A political controversy emerged after DPR Speaker Puan Maharani's name was absent from a commitment letter regarding the Asset Forfeiture Bill, with PDI-P defending the decision by stating the DPR operates collectively and collegially.
  • The Constitutional Court changed the rules for declaring national disasters, requiring at least three indicators to be met before such a designation can be made.
  • The Home Affairs Ministry awarded high-performing local governments in the Java-Bali region Batch II 2026 to encourage regional performance and innovation.
  • A district court rejected a pretrial motion by Febrie against the Attorney General's Office, ruling the suspect designation valid in a money laundering case dating to 2018.
  • State-owned shipping company PELNI partnered with the Corruption Eradication Commission to monitor fuel refilling for pioneer ships.

Foreign Policy & Defence

The Indonesian Army and US Army concluded a 15-day joint combat exercise in South Sumatra aimed at strengthening readiness in the Indo-Pacific region. The exercise was designed to enhance preparedness for both militaries in responding to regional security challenges.

  • Japan's Ministry of Defense dispatched three Chinook helicopters to assist Indonesia in combating forest and land fires in Kalimantan.
  • Timor-Leste's president invited President Prabowo for an official visit, and an Indonesian official stated that Papua can drive closer ties between the two nations.
  • Indonesia and Chile strengthened sanitary and phytosanitary cooperation to expand agricultural trade between the two countries.
  • Indonesia's ambassador appreciated the election of Kazakhstan's first female parliament speaker, and attended a parliamentary speakers conference calling for peaceful dispute resolution.

Other

Bank Indonesia revealed that 25 banks are still parking large amounts of funds in securities rather than lending, raising concerns about credit intermediation. The Financial Services Authority (OJK) urged Indonesians not to wait until they have substantial funds before beginning to save, and separately announced it targets 98 percent financial inclusion by 2045.

  • The government is preparing reconstruction plans for Sade Village after a devastating fire, and set Rp 3 million aid for disaster-hit micro businesses in Sumatra.
  • Indonesia prepared a 3S strategy to help young workers adapt to artificial intelligence in the workplace.
  • President Prabowo invited Nobel laureates to collaborate with Indonesian researchers, and separately Titiek Soeharto welcomed Nobel laureates and world figures at an event in Lampung.
  • The Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs inaugurated the Garuda Spark Innovation Hub in BSD City to strengthen the digital ecosystem toward global markets.
  • The Environment and Forestry Ministry sealed a factory waste channel suspected of polluting the Porong River.
